p.i: de simplicit. medicam. ubi docet discernere, facileque cognoscere alimenta bona & mala, si quis diligentius inspexerit, intelliget coturnicem praesertim assam boni gratique odoris esse & saporis, ac boni etiam nutrimenti. Illud quoque non omiserim, DEVM Israelis populum, quem ardentissime diligebat, dum per deserta illa transfiret loca, ad satietatem usque coturnicibus pasturum non fuisse, nisi probati illa fuissent alimenti & salutaris.

Quid multa ? Coturnices bene in ven-triculo confici, inque corporis alimoniam verti probæ temperaturæ & substantiæ indicium est. Nam in omnibus cibis ad boni succi generationem tantum requiritur, ut probe in ventriculo concoquantur, quicquid enim venter concoxerit, ad jecur transit, ab hoc veroBonus ad nutriendum partes transmittitur.cibus in

page.notes: The marginal notes on the right are short side-notes: Bonus, cibus in, ventre, probe, confecta (printed confect with a superscript a, read as uncertain), bonum, creat, succum. Each is placed beside the line where it stands. The line "satietatem usque" carries a dash-like mark after "satietatem" that looks like a rule rather than a line-end hyphen; it is transcribed without a hyphen. The word "concoctio" ends with a double full stop as printed. The running head is printed as "PROROGANDA." and is copied as it stands. The first line is a fragment continuing from the previous page.
